item.title: Cakacaka takes helm as General Manager of Nanuku Resort Fiji
item.description: Fijian hospitality leader Vuli Cakacaka has been appointed General Manager of Nanuku Resort Fiji. Cakacaka, who was born on Vatoa in the Lau Group and raised in Suva, has more than 23 years of experience in the hospitality industry, working across Fiji and international markets.
item.content:encoded:
Fijian hospitality leader Vuli Cakacaka has been appointed General Manager of Nanuku Resort Fiji.

Cakacaka, who was born on Vatoa in the Lau Group and raised in Suva, has more than 23 years of experience in the hospitality industry, working across Fiji and international markets.

He brings extensive experience and leadership expertise to the position.

He joined Nanuku Resort Fiji as Resort Manager in 2024 and will now oversee all aspects of resort operations, guest experience and financial performance as General Manager.

Cakacaka says the true strength of a resort lies in the people who deliver the experience.

He says he is honoured to lead the team and build on the strong foundation already established at Nanuku while continuing to provide personalised luxury.

He says the resort will continue creating meaningful experiences for guests while celebrating Fiji's culture, people and natural beauty.

Cakacaka is also committed to developing Fijian hospitality professionals and creating opportunities for local talent.

Storey Hospitality Co-founder and Managing Partner Michael Casey says Cakacaka's extensive experience, understanding of Fijian hospitality and people-first leadership make him the right person to lead the resort.

Casey says they look forward to the continued growth and success of Nanuku under Cakacaka's leadership.

Located on Fiji's southern coast in Pacific Harbour, Nanuku Resort Fiji is celebrated for its luxury experiences, authentic cultural connections and exceptional service.

The resort remains dedicated to delivering unforgettable stays while championing sustainability, community engagement and world-class hospitality.

item.title: TotalEnergies relaunches first directly operated service station in Nabua
item.description: TotalEnergies Fiji Managing Director Bhavna Samel says the Nabua outlet is the company's first service station in Fiji to be both owned and directly operated by TotalEnergies. Samel says the relaunch is an emotional milestone for the company as the Nabua outlet becomes its first directly operated service station in the country.
item.content:encoded:
TotalEnergies Fiji Managing Director Bhavna Samel says the Nabua outlet is the company's first service station in Fiji to be both owned and directly operated by TotalEnergies.

Samel says the relaunch is an emotional milestone for the company as the Nabua outlet becomes its first directly operated service station in the country.

She says the station has undergone a complete redevelopment, including new pipes, tanks, pumps, shop facilities and other infrastructure.

Sam says TotalEnergies wants the Nabua outlet to become a model service station in terms of customer service, technology and facilities.

The redeveloped station also includes a car wash, lube bay and food and coffee services, giving motorists access to a range of services at one location.

Sam says this is the sixth TotalEnergies service station to undergo major renovation in Fiji as the company continues to invest in its local network.

She says the company is working towards providing similar standards across its service stations.

French Embassy Chargé d'Affaires Benjamin Delannoy says continued investment by French companies such as TotalEnergies creates jobs, supports local businesses and suppliers, and provides opportunities for skills development.

Delannoy says TotalEnergies has 35 service stations in Fiji and five in Tonga, serving thousands of customers each day.

He says the relaunch of the Nabua station reflects the company's continued confidence in Fiji and strengthens economic ties between Fiji and Franc e .

item.title: Fijians urged by LICI to consider adequate life insurance cover
item.description: Fijians are being encouraged to consider whether they have adequate life insurance cover as insurance penetration in the country remains below two percent. This was stressed by LICI General Manager Shridhar Pathare during the company's 70th anniversary celebrations, saying insurance density stands at about $210 in premiums per person.
item.content:encoded:
Fijians are being encouraged to consider whether they have adequate life insurance cover as insurance penetration in the country remains below two percent.

This was stressed by LICI General Manager Shridhar Pathare during the company's 70th anniversary celebrations, saying insurance density stands at about $210 in premiums per person.

Pathare says there is significant room for growth in Fiji, with many people either not having life insurance or potentially being underinsured.

LICI Fiji currently has more than 62,000 policyholders and more than 200 agents, with four offices and five sales service centres around the country.

He says the company's assets have reached almost $1.05 billion.

LICI also generated a valuation surplus of $27 million last year, with Pathare saying 95 percent was distributed among policyholders.

Pathare highlights that LICI settled around 174 death claims last year and paid $4.74 million to nominees, adding that these payments provide financial support to families following the deaths of policyholders.

LICI also settled more than 1,200 maturity claims last year, distributing $23.91 million, while 5,619 policies received survival benefits totalling $18.90 million.

Meanwhile, LICI IT Manager K. Raveendra says the company has not faced difficulties managing accident-related claims despite concerns about the increasing number of road accidents.

Raveendra says that over the last five years, LICI has recorded around 180 death claims among its policyholder base of about 62,000.

He says about 20 to 25 of those were accident benefit claims, representing less than 0.2 percent of the company's policyholder base.

He says policyholders with accident benefit riders can receive an additional payment in the event of an accident, depending on their cover.

LICI HR Manager Vivek Prakash says the company also offers rider benefits for an additional premium.

Prakash says one of these is the double accident benefit rider, which provides additional benefits relating to accidents and can also cover disability due to an accident or illness.

Pathare also highlighted LICI's investments in Fiji Infrastructure Bonds.

He says the market value of the company's investment in Fiji Infrastructure Bonds stood at $943 million as of 31st December 2025, while a further $56 million has been invested so far this year.

Pathare says these investments channel policyholders' savings into projects that strengthen roads, schools, hospitals and communities.

Me anwhile, LICI, which began operations in India on 1st September 1956, started operating in Fiji on 5th October 1956 and will mark 70 years of operations in the country next month.

The company is also marking its 70th anniversary with community initiatives, including support for charitable organisations, elderly care facilities and schools.
